chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Chubby Jackson's influence and limits as a musician
summary: Herman calls Chubby Jackson a strong influence and spark plug for the band, but says his lack of continued musical study limited him as music grew complex.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: How about Chubby's role? Now, he went through quite a number of (Inaudible) more than a decade.

Oh, yeah. Well, mostly Chubby was a very strong and good -- a very strong influence, first of all, and in most cases, very good. I think, though, that somewhere along the line, his not continuing his musical -- let's put it bluntly, his musical education --

-- that music got too complex and that's when he left the scene, really, for any great intent. I think he still is a guy that certainly can swing a band and can help to swing a band and has generally very good musical taste.
But there's always going to be certain things that

he's not going to be ready to do because he didn't study enough to be able to facilitate the whole thing. And that's unfortunate in his case, because if Ray Brown is still an important bassist, then Chubby certainly should be.
Well, he was one of the spark plugs for kind of the spirit in the band.
Oh, yes, definitely. And he would still be, if he were there. Or anywhere. Wherever he is, there's a spark plug.
